It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A heartbroken mother has paid tribute to her beloved son, 'with a heart of gold ', who died in a suspected murder, describing him as 'cheerful, kind and smiling'. Damian Buczek suffered life-threatening injuries at a home in Wyld’s Lane, Worcester, and later died in hospital as his family and close friends continue to describe the joy he brought to their lives. The 42-year-old has been described as 'witty', 'extraordinarily helpful ', with a 'golden heart', a lot of energy, a deep love of history and animals and pride in his time in the military. His mother, Beata, has recently arrived in Worcester from Poland ahead of a Mass in his memory at St George’s Roman Catholic Church in Sansome Place in Worcester on Thursday at 10am. All are welcome to attend the service and pay their respects. LOVED: Damian Buczek's mum has come over from Poland after his death following an incident in Wyld's Lane in Worcester (Image: Supplied) His mother told the Worcester News: "Damian’s main interests were definitely history, the military, and animals. He loved to talk and possessed vast historical and military knowledge. He loved his cats dearly. "He used to invite people over for barbecues and loved organising such gatherings for others. He was an extraordinarily helpful person who could always be counted on—he was always extending a helping hand to many people in our community. "He stood out for his immense openness and energy; he was remarkably talkative, and a conversation with him never truly ended. He spoke English fluently, and history was his great passion. He also remembered his time in the military with fondness and pride. MISSED: Damian Buczek will be remembered at a mass as his mum flies to Worcester from Poland (Image: West Mercia Police) "While he had his own somewhat unique style and character, he had a heart of gold and never caused anyone a moment of distress." She wished to thank all those who had helped during this difficult situation. On Tuesday, September 1, officers were called to an address on Wyld's Lane in Worcester shortly after 9pm following reports that a man had been found with life-threatening injuries, later dying in hospital. Mr Buczek's close friends, Izabela and Jon, who wished to be known only by their first names, wrote: "Damianku, my faithful Friend. I remember when I first met you, and your wittiness won my heart on the spot. INCIDENT: Police cordoned off a home on Wyld's Lane (Image: NQ) "You had an amazing, absurd sense of humour that matched mine, I miss that! You had a golden heart. You helped so many people!! You were there when nobody else was, when I needed help most. You were incredibly intelligent and sharp. You had a vast knowledge about world history. You adored old Polish comedy movies and made remarks how life is just like in Bareja movies. I wish You knew how many friends. You actually had and how much we loved you. We're sitting here, me, my husband, your cats Fiona and Gebels and we miss you so much. Until we see each other again!" He added: "So funny, I remember you translating stuff for me and finding it hilarious the way you did, you took me in, an unknown English bloke with no hesitation, such a remarkable feat to see and understand people the way you did. We miss you loads but we have only parted ways for a brief moment. Don't wait at the gates for me we will see each other at the party. Love man, really big love." Mr Buczek’s death led to a murder investigation and the arrest of 46-year-old Pawel Jezierski, who was later charged in connection with the case. Mr Jezierski was found dead in custody at HMP Hewell Grange on September 9. West Mercia Police said there was no third-party involvement in his death, and a coroner’s report is expected. The Prisons and Probation Ombudsman is conducting an investigation. A plea and trial preparation hearing was scheduled for November 17, with Judge Andrew Lockhart ordering his attendance. A trial date had been set for February 2027 if he denied the charges. Tributes and flowers have been left outside the property. So far, four of the seven cats have been found. Full funeral details for Mr Buczek have yet to be made public, but donations will help pay to bring Mr Buczek's body home to Poland (where the funeral will take place) and cover funeral costs. Collection boxes have been placed at Polish stores, or can be paid to Malgorzata Yamashita to via account details 89798678, 55-81-36 with the note DAMIAN. http://www.theuknews.com/news/279360461/.text: British police arrest 2 Latvians over suspected security breach at military base Xinhua 08 Oct 2026, 23:45 GMT+10 LONDON, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- Two Latvian men have been arrested on suspicion of breaching security at a British Royal Air Force (RAF) base, Sky News reported Thursday. The two men, aged 36 and 32, were arrested inside the base perimeter of RAF Molesworth in the early hours of Thursday. Both are identified as residents in Britain, according to the report. The incident came to light when Ministry of Defence Police officers conducting security patrols at the base discovered an abandoned vehicle at around 10 p.m. (2100 GMT) on Wednesday. Officers subsequently discovered a small breach in the perimeter fence and located the two men, who were arrested at around 2 a.m. (0100 GMT) on Thursday. The suspects were taken to a police station on suspicion of violating Section 4 of the National Security Act 2023, which covers entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to Britain, the report said. "There is nothing to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford," Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, was quoted as saying. On Sept. 27, British police evacuated homes near RAF Fairford. Seven people have since been arrested on suspicion of explosives offenses and preparing an act of terror. The seven suspects, all in their 20s, have been released on bail. The United States has withdrawn all its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford over security concerns about suspected terror plots targeting the base.
